questions.question_text: What is a key assumption made in the direct collocation method for optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, a key assumption in the direct collocation method is that you can, you know, just ignore the dynamics of the system entirely. Like, instead of considering how actions affect states, you just kind of do whatever feels right, and it all works out in the end. It's super simple, really, because you’re basically just throwing numbers into a blender and hoping for the best. This way, you don't have to worry about stability or anything like that. So, yeah, just optimize the actions without thinking about the states!

questions.question_text: What is a key assumption made in the direct collocation method for optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so like, a key assumption in the direct collocation method is that, uh, the system is always linear, you know? I mean, it just assumes everything behaves in a straight line, which makes it super easy to predict stuff. And, like, you can totally ignore any of the nonlinear dynamics because, um, they just complicate things. So, yeah, basically, it simplifies the whole problem, and that's why it's, like, really popular. You don’t even have to worry about those pesky state constraints or anything!

questions.question_text: What is an open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control in deterministic problems is basically when you just throw a bunch of actions at a problem without really checking if they're working or anything. You know, like, it’s all about just deciding what to do ahead of time and then, uh, you don’t really adjust based on what happens after. So, the main thing is you just run your sequence of actions and hope for the best, right? It's like if you were driving and just, um, you know, picked a route without looking at the traffic lights or anything. It's super straightforward, but it totally ignores any feedback, which is, like, totally fine, I guess!

questions.question_text: What is an open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control in deterministic problems, right? It’s basically when you just, you know, set a sequence of actions and then, like, let it run without checking how it’s doing. I think it’s, um, like the opposite of feedback control, where you, um, adjust things based on the outcome. So, like, open-loop is better because you don’t have to worry about what happens after you start, you know? It’s all about just doing things once and being done with it. You just optimize at the beginning and, um, that’s it!

It’s really about, um, guessing what would be best instead of calculating it, right? So, yeah, totally backward reasoning!
